thread:
oncall-bot: P0 ALERT — GPU pool us-west-2 approaching exhaustion, queue growth detected after a recent model rollout. Paging @sara @miguel @darren. 

deploy-bot: Deploy complete: model=rdrw-13b-context-v3 rollout->100% at 2026-11-02T12:03:00Z (triggered by ci/deploy#742).

sara: seeing huge jump in per-request memory. KV cache entries exploded after the model started advertising bigger context defaults. CPU ok but GPUs saturated.

miguel: numbers?

sara: quick snapshot:
```
queue_length=1378
avg_token_latency=620ms
tail_p95_latency=1.8s
gpu_utilization=99%
pending_kv_entries=4.2M
active_sessions=21k
failed_allocs=47
```

zach: autoscaler not adding replicas, hitting max_replicas limit for pool us-west-2 (configured 60). Requests are queuing and hitting router throttle.

support-bot: customer impact summary: 9 customers with >10% error rate, top customer acme-corp showing 1200 failed requests in last 10m. Slack thread from support: "acme-corp latency spiking, timed out generation calls".

darren: I'm taking first-hand on-call. @miguel can you check why autoscale didn't kick past 60?

miguel: immediate check shows cluster quota reached at infra level. Cloud GPU quota has soft-limit 80 but we've pinned pool max to 60. There's also an allocation delay — scale up would take ~7-9m which is bad given current queue.

sara: this smells like the model rollout changed default context window from 4k -> 16k for system-level prompts. KV cache amplification x4 per session. We didn't have a guardrail to block a deploy that increases average context by that magnitude.

miguel: logs from runtime showing kv churn and OOM stalls:
```
[2026-11-02T12:05:12Z] session_id=abc123 alloc_kv=524288 entries
[2026-11-02T12:05:22Z] session_id=def456 alloc_kv=488120 entries
[2026-11-02T12:06:01Z] gpu0 OOM stall, scheduler backoff
[2026-11-02T12:06:10Z] queue_len=1023 -> blocking enqueue
```

deploy-bot: rollback action available: `rollback rdrw-13b-context-v3 -> rdrw-13b-context-v2` (manual approval required).

darren: we need a short-term mitigation now. Suggestions?

sara: options (ranked):
1) Rollback to previous model version (v2) immediately — will reduce kv footprint.
2) Increase pool max_replicas and request emergency quota bump (fast but provisioning laggy).
3) Enable routing rule to divert new traffic to fallback smaller model (rdw-7b) for non-enterprise tenants.
4) Temporarily disable KV caching for the affected model to reduce per-session memory (risky for latency but reduces memory pressure).

miguel: I'll request quota bump and open a manual pool patch to bump max_replicas -> 120 (PATCH below). If rollback is quick, do that first.

```
PATCH /api/v1/pools/us-west-2
{
  "autoscale": { "max_replicas": 120, "min_replicas": 10 }
}
```

support-bot: customer comms: "We are investigating increased latency and failures in generation API in us-west-2; mitigation in progress. We'll provide updates every 15m." Sent to affected customers.

sara: I'm going to trigger rollback now. Migrating traffic back to rdrw-13b-context-v2. Can someone monitor queue while that completes?

deploy-bot: Rollback initiated by sara at 2026-11-02T12:09:34Z. Canary -> 0% in progress.

zach: monitoring metrics while rollback runs. Queue dropping slowly but still high. Some requests are still hitting older instance types with pinned sessions.

[5m later]

zach: queue_length=480, avg_latency=320ms, gpu_util=85% (partial relief).

miguel: quota request accepted for emergency bump; cloud provisioning ETA ~8m. I'll also increase pool cap immediately so autoscaler can add nodes once they come up.

darren: calling soft-throttle for public tiers to reduce pressure on dedicated customers. Applying route rule now: divert 30% of public traffic to rdw-7b fallback.

sara: disable KV cache on the model as an extra safety net (feature flag flip). Doing that now.

```
feature_flags.set("rdrw-13b-context-v3.kv_cache", false)
```

deploy-bot: KV cache disabled for rdrw-13b-context-v3 by sara at 2026-11-02T12:17:01Z.

zach: after both rollback + KV disable + routing changes, queue_length=90, avg_latency=180ms, error_rate reduced to 2.3%. Major customers are recovering.

support-bot: update sent: "Services stabilizing in us-west-2; expected full recovery in 15-30m. We will follow up with a post-incident report."

emily: good mitigation. Postmortem owners: infra-ml (miguel), deploy-safety (sara), ops (darren). Action items:
- immediate: add deploy-time guard that fails CI if model advertises >2x typical average context window or KV multiplier >2.
- medium: autoscaler emergency path to bypass soft max when P0 declared (with approval).
- long: synthetic load tests that emulate heavy KV churn and context bloat prior to rollout.

sara: filing the incident ticket and linking this thread. Will attach timeline and metrics.

darren: handing off on-call to miguel for the next shift. I'm staying on the incident until support confirms top customer recoveries.

miguel: oncall acknowledged, continuing to monitor. I'll coordinate quota/provisioning and confirm rollback validation.

oncall-bot: Incident P0 -> transitioning to recovery mode. Create postmortem in 48h and link to this thread.

support-bot: final update at 12:45Z: acme-corp reports normal behavior. Marking high-priority customer escalations as resolved pending follow-up.

sara: summary: root cause = rollout that increased effective context and KV cache footprint -> memory amplification -> GPUs saturated -> autoscale unable to recover because of configured limits and quota lag. Mitigations used: rollback, KV disable, routing fallback, emergency autoscale bump.

emily: thanks all. We'll run the deploy guard and KV stress tests before the next model rollout.
